title: McKenzie Method: Mechanical Diagnosis and Therapy (MDT)

blocks.text: MDT uses repeated movements and sustained positions to classify patients by their symptom and movement response. The most important concepts:

items: **Centralisation**: referred symptoms retreat toward the spine (for example leg pain shrinks to the buttock, then the back) during repeated movement in one direction. Centralisation is associated with a better prognosis [Ref – to verify].
**Directional preference**: one direction of movement improves symptoms and range, the opposite worsens them.

rows: Rapid changes in symptoms and range with repeated movements; directional preference; centralisation
Repeated movements in the preferred direction; avoid the opposite direction temporarily
Pain only at end range of a shortened tissue, consistent, no rapid change
Repeated end-range movement in the painful direction to remodel tissue
Pain only with sustained end-range posture, no movement loss
Does not fit, including serious pathology, stenosis, chronic pain

items: Baseline: symptoms (location, intensity) and a mechanical baseline (range, SLR).
Repeated flexion in standing (10 reps), then reassess.
Repeated extension in standing (10 reps), reassess.
Repeated flexion in lying, extension in lying (prone press-ups), side-glides if needed.
Interpret: does a direction centralise, decrease or abolish symptoms and improve range? That is the directional preference.
Prone lying, then prone on elbows, then prone press-ups: 10 reps every 2 to 3 hours.
Progress force: therapist overpressure, extension mobilisation if needed.
Recovery of function, then movement in other directions as tolerated.

blocks.text: Stop if symptoms peripheralise (spread further into the limb) or neurological signs worsen. Screen red flags first.

items: **What is centralisation?** Referred symptoms moving toward the spine with repeated movement.
**Why is it important?** It is associated with better outcomes and guides treatment direction.
**What does peripheralisation mean?** Symptoms spreading further into the limb: stop or change direction.
**Which syndrome shows rapid change with repeated movements?** Derangement.
**How often are home exercises usually performed?** Often every 2 to 3 hours in the early phase.
